v1.18.0 closes the 1.17 series. The series was short and was about the ground the product stands
on rather than the product: search runs on OpenSearch 3.7, upgraded in place from 2.19 with the
tooling to do it again; the service runs on Python 3.14, with the one dependency the move forced;
and the graph tier carries the changes the coming engine upgrade wants on the image before the
engine itself moves. No endpoint, model or field changed. The 1.18 line that opens here returns to
the product — consolidation across the companies a graph holds, and the accounting features that
follow from keeping several sets of books in one place.

Covers everything since v1.17.0; the 1.17.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## Search on OpenSearch 3.7

The domain moved from 2.19 to 3.7 in place. Three things made that a deploy rather than a rebuild.
The template now declares the domain upgradable: without that, CloudFormation treats an engine
change as a replacement, the fixed domain name refuses it, and the stack rolls back having moved
nothing. The deploy workflow's monitor can outlive the one-hour session the deploy role is allowed —
it watches for 55 minutes, takes fresh credentials, and watches again — and it reports an expired
session as what it is rather than as a missing stack. And 2.19 is retired as a version anything new
reads: the template's default and only allowed value is 3.7, the deploy inputs and their fallbacks
say 3.7, and the local stack runs the 3.x image. A stale `2.19` now fails parameter validation
instead of attempting a downgrade.

The index mapping changed with the engine. OpenSearch 3.6 and later require the fp16 encoder to
state its width, so the mapping carries `bits: 16` beside the encoder type. The index created on
2.19 was never affected, but without this no new index could be created on 3.7 — the
rebuild-from-source path included — and the first write would have auto-created one with a dynamic
mapping that loses the vector type. No mapping satisfies both engines, which is why the change
waited for production to be confirmed on 3.7.

Three admin commands came with the upgrade. `search settings` reads the live index settings and
flags anything the 3.x pre-upgrade check would refuse, across every index the name resolves to.
`search warmup` loads the k-NN graphs into memory so the first query after a restart does not pay
for the load. `search memory-optimized on|off|status` turns the memory-optimized k-NN mode (3.1+)
on or off for the index; the setting is static, so the command closes and reopens the index, and
reopens it even when the update fails.

## The runtime: Python 3.14

The API, the workers, the orchestrator and the Lambda image run on Python 3.14, as a single
version. 3.13 moved to security-only this month, and everything in the lock already resolved and
passed on 3.14, so the move is the pins — the interpreter, both image stages, the Lambda base and
its managed runtime, the workflows — and a tree written for it: the formatter's 3.14 target drops
the parentheses from exception tuples and the quotes from forward-reference annotations across
about a hundred files, and the two calls the interpreter now deprecates are gone.

One dependency moved because 3.14 forced it. dbt-core 1.11 caps mashumaro below the first release
that runs on 3.14, and the QuickBooks transform asset shells out to `dbt build`, so the held 1.12
line is now required: dbt-core 1.12.6, dbt-adapters 1.24.5, mashumaro 3.17, and the metricflow
subtree that 1.12 declares as a hard dependency, which is most of the roughly 200 MB the API image
grew by. Nothing else changed version for the move.

The published packages followed. `robosystems-client` 2.14.3 and `xbrlkit` 0.21.3 are the first
releases of each to declare 3.14 and the first with a floor of 3.12: a 3.11 consumer of the client
stays on 2.14.2, a pip user of xbrlkit on 3.10 or 3.11 stays on 0.21.2, and `uvx` users are
unaffected because uv fetches a matching interpreter. Both are the versions this release locks.

## Ahead of the LadybugDB engine upgrade

Four changes the engine upgrade wants on the image before the engine moves, all running on the
current engine, so the image a rollback lands on already carries them. The connection pool refuses
a database file that does not exist rather than letting the engine create an empty one; files are
created only by `create_database` and the migration import, and every Graph API route opens
through the pool. The read guard's label deny list covers the engine's catalog labels at every site
that composes the analyzer's predicates — the statement kernel, the MCP read and subgraph-write
tools, and the Graph API's own validator — and sees a quoted label as the label it is; a graph's
schema is read through the schema endpoints. A tuning parameter for the engine's plan cache,
`graph/ENGINE_PLAN_CACHE_MODE` (`READS`, `WRITES`, `BOTH`, `NONE`; empty keeps the engine
default), is applied per connection in its own block, so an engine without the setting keeps the
rest of its tuning. And the tests that wrote fixed temporary database paths use per-run paths, so
two engine versions on one machine no longer upgrade each other's files.

The engine upgrade itself is not in this release. It ships as its own release once the next engine
line has settled, because an engine upgrade changes the on-disk format and so has a different
rollback than code.

## API surface changes

None. No endpoint, model or field changed, and nothing reaches either client SDK; the rewrites
under the routers are syntax only.

## Deploying this release

- **No migrations** on either database.
- **CloudFormation stack updates**: `graph-infra`, whose inline API-key generator function moves to
  the `python3.14` managed runtime with its code unchanged, and `opensearch`, a no-op on a domain
  already on 3.7.
- **The images are a new interpreter.** The API, worker and orchestrator images are on 3.14 and
  about 200 MB larger, so expect longer pulls on the first deploy. The one 3.14 runtime change that
  can bite a service — Linux `multiprocessing` defaulting to forkserver — is not relied on by
  anything here (the orchestrator's executor pins spawn; the API runs single-process), but the
  orchestrator daemon and worker logs are the place to look after the deploy.
- **A new tuning parameter**, optional: `graph/ENGINE_PLAN_CACHE_MODE`, read when the Graph API
  starts; unset keeps the engine default.
- **Locally**: `just rebuild` for the 3.14 image, and `docker compose pull opensearch` to move the
  search container to the 3.x image. A 3.x engine reads a volume created by 2.x, and the volume is
  rebuildable if not.
